findings.title: The `scorecard` emit field is required by the renderer but never declared by the emit-shape owner
findings.recommendation: Strict validation checks internal emits for 'the scorecard shape' and the spine-facts contract computes final_assessment 'from the emit's own scorecard' — but the persisted-summary scenario still enumerates 'findings summary (counts by severity and by pass)' and the schema reference (review.ts:27,53) documents findings_summary with NO scorecard field; task 3.4's edits don't add it. A producer following the schema emits records the renderer rejects — every run-and-paste loop fails. (Live practice already diverged: recent emits carry scorecard and omit findings_summary; orbit-conventions:209's editorial-kind findings_summary line is the un-delta'd neighbor.) Name the 3-dimension×severity scorecard in the persisted-content list; extend task 3.4 to declare scorecard in references/run-summary-schema.md and state findings_summary's status (trail.ts:143-152 already falls back to counting findings[]); reconcile orbit-conventions:209.

iteration_note: Note: 0 of these findings appeared in prior runs. 7 new this run (trend: 16 → 12-external → 7, severity now 1C/2W/4S — the CRITICAL count falling 5 → 7 → 1). The independent pass verified the ENTIRE external iter-2 batch landed and mutually consistent (all 7 CRITICAL resolutions checked at their exact sites; all 12 MODIFIED blocks diffed baseline-verbatim; the collapse's predicates verified live in engine-gates; carriers 20/20; fingerprints 12/12; grounding code confirmed). The remaining findings are third-order: the schema REFERENCE the emit-shape scenario cites never declared the scorecard field the renderer now requires (live practice had silently diverged from that reference for cycles — D4's strictness makes the divergence load-bearing), plus two un-delta'd neighbors of the collapse and four polish items.
commentary: The pattern across the three passes is a tightening spiral: iter 1 caught the baseline text describing the replaced machinery, iter 2 caught contradictions between the iter-1 resolutions and the layers (templates, prompt contracts) the sweep missed, and this pass caught the seams between the NEW contracts and their un-delta'd neighbors — the schema reference nobody had read against the renderer's validation, the engine-gates citation into deleted text, the conventions example written under the old voice. The CRITICAL is the interesting one: the schema reference and live emit practice had ALREADY diverged (emits carry scorecard; the reference documents findings_summary), harmlessly — D4's strict validation is what turns that latent divergence into a hard failure, which is the determinism thesis working exactly as intended, one layer earlier than expected.
